newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OPEC sees no major impact on market from Iraqi oil.
newsitem.headline: OPEC sees no major impact on market from Iraqi oil.

text.p: OPEC Secretary-General Rilwanu Lukman on Tuesday said he was confident the oil market would manage to absorb Iraqi crude when it returns to the market and forecast there would be little impact on prices.
Oil prices dipped briefly on Monday on news that Iraqi state-owned oil company SOMO had already signed contracts with some foreign companies to sell oil under the delayed U.N. "oil-for-food" plan.
"The market is always nervous," Lukman told reporters during a break in a three-day gas and technology conference.
"It looks as though the market has largely discounted any impact from the re-introduction of Iraqi oil...We are only talking about another 700,000 or so barrels per day."
Asked when he thought Iraqi oil might reenter the market, Lukman said: "Most people say hopefully by the end of the year, or in the first quarter of 1997."
Iraqi oil exports have been banned under a U.N. embargo imposed after Iraq invaded Kuwait in 1990.
The Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Companies last week agreed to roll over its production ceiling of 25.03 million barrels per day until next June.
